subject: Dedicated reserved-commit options & ramp schedule for ZeppelinAI
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@zeppelin.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reserved-commit options & ramp schedule for ZeppelinAI

Hi Sara — great talking yesterday. Thanks for the context on Zeppelin's Q4 inference roadmap. Per our discussion, attaching a concise set of reserved-commit proposals so your finance and platform teams can compare. High-level items: 

- Three term options (12/24/36 months) with step-down unit pricing tied to committed GPU-hours.
- Two ramp profiles: "Frontloaded" (50% capacity in month 1 -> full by month 3) and "Even ramp" (linear over first 6 months).
- Throughput guarantees scoped per model family; we can set per-route SLOs and objective burst windows.

Quick questions for alignment before we lock prices:
1) Do you need a hard start date (contractually guaranteed) or is a "target start" with confirmed capacity windows acceptable?
2) Will Zeppelin want a separate SLA for latency percentiles on critical routes (e.g., 95th p50/p95)?
3) Preferred billing cadence (monthly invoice vs. quarterly in arrears)?

I've attached the pricing options and a draft SOW. If it helps we can produce a side-by-side TCO for your MAAP workloads. Can Karthik and Marissa join a short call tomorrow to walk through the mechanics?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Options_v2.pdf, Draft_SOW_Redwood-Zeppelin.docx

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@zeppelin.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved-commit options & ramp schedule for ZeppelinAI

Thanks Olga — appreciate the clear options. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Finance prefers a 24- or 36-month commit but needs to see a material discount for 36 months. Our internal threshold for 'material' is ~18-22% net vs. list.
- We have a locked pen-testing window late Oct; a firm capacity start by 2026-11-01 would be ideal. If that's not feasible, a target window of Nov–Dec is workable but we'd need credit protections.
- For SLAs: we require a 95th percentile latency SLA for our real-time routing (model family: z-rt-1). Also need a throughput guarantee: sustained 1200 tokens/sec for z-rt-1 during business hours with burst to 3000 tokens/sec for 10 minutes.

I'll loop in our procurement alias (salesops@zeppelin.ai) once we have exact pricing and a DocuSign-ready SOW. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports a phased start with explicit credits for missed milestones?

— Sara
Head of Platform Engineering | ZeppelinAI

On Tue, Sep 8, 2026 at 09:55 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sara / Olga — adding the pricing math below so finance has something concrete. I can join any call today or tomorrow.
>
> 1) 12-month term: list $0.90/committed GPU-hour (baseline), 8% discount on list for minimum 1.5x baseline throughput commitment.
> 2) 24-month term: list $0.82/committed GPU-hour, 14% discount with 1.2x throughput commitment.
> 3) 36-month term: list $0.75/committed GPU-hour, 22% discount with 1.1x throughput commitment + optional 3 month price protection for quantization changes.
>
> Ramp proposals (example for a 100 GPU-hour/day target):
> - Frontloaded: Month 1: 50 GPU-hr/day, Month 2: 80, Month 3+: 100
> - Even ramp: increase ~17 GPU-hr/day each month to reach 100 by month 6
>
> Contractual start date: we can commit to a firm start if you choose the 36-month + frontloaded ramp; otherwise we recommend a target window and include milestone credits (1% monthly credit up to 6% total if start slips beyond agreed date).
>
> I'll also attach a sample SLA excerpt and a short table that maps committed GPU-hours to expected token throughput for common model families.
>
> — Karthik
> Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@zeppelin.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved-commit options & ramp schedule for ZeppelinAI

Sara — following up with a slightly more prescriptive commercial alternative that often helps procurement compare scenarios quickly.

Option A (Balanced): 24-month commit, even ramp over 4 months, 14% effective discount. Start date: target 2026-11-01 with contractual milestone credits (1.5% per month beyond start, capped at 6%). Throughput guarantee: 95th percentile latency commitment + sustained 1200 tokens/sec; quarterly load tests carve out for verification.

Option B (Aggressive savings): 36-month commit, frontloaded ramp, 22% discount, firm start date 2026-11-01 with a 30-day SLA remedy credit (applies if throughput not met during first 3 months). We can also include a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the first-year commit if Zeppelin agrees to the 36-month term and a single invoice cadence (annual prepay).

Notes: 
- Onboarding and pre-provisioning: If you want a guaranteed capacity standby during pen-test windows, we recommend reserving a small buffer (10-15% above expected load) for the first 90 days.
- Quantization and model changes: we include a single compat check per major model version change; additional engineering hours are billable or convert into an annual support add-on.

If you want, I can translate Option B into a redline-ready SOW and a final quote for DocuSign.

— Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@zeppelin.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved-commit options & ramp schedule for ZeppelinAI

Sara — quick ops note from our side on SLAs and burst behavior so there are no surprises: 

- SLA measurement: p95 latency measured at the route-level (30s windows) with upstream retries excluded. Remedy credits are applied to monthly invoice and cannot exceed 25% of the monthly commit.
- Burst policy: 10-minute burst windows are supported using autoscaling subject to available headroom; guaranteed bursts require reserved buffer (we can reserve but it counts toward committed capacity).
- Start-date acceptance: we can accept a firm start date in the contract if Zeppelin selects Option B (36 months) — otherwise we'll list a target window with milestone credits as described.

I'll attach a short SLO excerpt to the SOW before DocuSign. Let me know if you want the SLO language tightened.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@zeppelin.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: salesops@zeppelin.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved-commit options & ramp schedule for ZeppelinAI

Thanks all — this is helpful and close to what procurement needs. A few next steps from Zeppelin: 

1) Procurement will run a quick internal cost-MOA and confirm whether 36-month at ~22% is acceptable; expect an answer by Fri EOD PT.
2) Please send the DocuSign-ready SOW and final quote (Option B + onboarding credit written into SOW) by EOD so we can route for signatures.
3) We will also share a redline with two small asks: explicit 11/01/2026 start date (conditional on payment schedule) and a maximum SLA credit cap of 10% (finance prefers a lower cap).

Once we have the signed SOW, we'll request a short security orientation call for late Oct pen-test scheduling.

— Sara
Head of Platform Engineering | ZeppelinAI

Attachments referenced: Zeppelin_MAAP_Budget.xlsx
